title: Quasar back-to-back sub-device tests results in Watcher corruption
body:
On Quasar, running sub-device tests back-to-back with Watcher enabled results in Watcher throwing a corruption error on the second test. The first test always seems to run fine. With Watcher disabled, all the sub-device tests pass. If only a single sub-device test runs with Watcher enabled, that test passes as well without any Watcher errors. The error only occurs when running multiple sub-device tests back-to-back with Watcher on.

With the help of AI, it seems that calling `overlay_cmd_buff_init(atomic_ret_val);` in `noc_init()` in `quasar/noc_nonblocking_api_v2.h` fixes this bug. I'm not sure whether this fix proposed by AI is actually the best way to fix this.

To repro:
1. `git checkout sagarwal/qsr_b2b_sub_device_tests_bug`
2. Build `tt-metal`
3. Make the `TT_METAL_SIMULATOR` env var point to `tt-umd-simulators/build/emu-quasar-2x3_DISPATCH/`
4. Run `TT_METAL_WATCHER=1 ./build/test/tt_metal/unit_tests_legacy --gtest_filter=*Quasar*SubDevice*`

On the second test, Watcher throws a corruption error:
```
2026-08-18 17:33:07.134 | critical |          Always | TT_THROW: Watcher found corruption at L1[0] on core 0-1: read 0 (assert.hpp:104)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  TT_THROW @ ../tt_metal/impl/debug/watcher_device_reader.cpp:711: tt::exception
info:
Watcher found corruption at L1[0] on core 0-1: read 0
backtrace:
 --- /localdev/sagarwal/worktree1/build_Debug/tt_metal/libtt_metal.so(+0x19c594b) [0x7f6b21ed694b]
 --- tt::tt_metal::WatcherDeviceReader::Core::DumpL1Status() const
 --- tt::tt_metal::WatcherDeviceReader::Core::Dump() const
 --- tt::tt_metal::WatcherDeviceReader::Dump(_IO_FILE*)
 --- tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl::dump(_IO_FILE*)
 --- /localdev/sagarwal/worktree1/build_Debug/tt_metal/libtt_metal.so(+0x1e3e19c) [0x7f6b2234f19c]
 --- tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl::poll_watcher_data()
 --- void std::__invoke_impl<void, void (tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl::*)(), tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl*>(std::__invoke_memfun_deref, void (tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl::*&&)(), tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl*&&)
 --- std::__invoke_result<void (tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl::*)(), tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl*>::type std::__invoke<void (tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl::*)(), tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl*>(void (tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl::*&&)(), tt::tt_metal::WatcherServer::Impl*&&)
 --- /localdev/sagarwal/worktree1/build_Debug/tt_metal/libtt_metal.so(+0x1e448a2) [0x7f6b223558a2]
 --- /localdev/sagarwal/worktree1/build_Debug/tt_metal/libtt_metal.so(+0x1e44865) [0x7f6b22355865]
 --- /localdev/sagarwal/worktree1/build_Debug/tt_metal/libtt_metal.so(+0x1e44749) [0x7f6b22355749]
 --- /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6(+0xdc253) [0x7f6b1f378253]
 --- /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3) [0x7f6b1effeac3]
 --- /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x1268d0) [0x7f6b1f0908d0]
```

In the branch, if you uncomment the `overlay_cmd_buff_init(atomic_ret_val);` in `noc_init()` and re-run, all the tests pass with Watcher enabled.
